title: Tinn — source-first mechanical sailplane
status: Educational engineering completion; not a recovered buildable design or validated flight prediction.
source_review: All nine supplied photographs were read directly for this implementation. Printed text is distinguished below from uncertain marginal handwriting.

source_geometry.excluded: The original 3.135 ft wing-length conversion is inconsistent with the metric and adjacent imperial entries. The later comparison AR 7.83 is not substituted for the requested original area paragraph.

photographs.reading: Mute swan planform: broad arm wing and approximately elliptical outer outline. Say span 7.4 ft, wrist span 3.7 ft = 50% b. Original paragraph gives total area 6.61 ft² and AR about 8.29; notes that outer area and spreading vary.
photographs.used: Scaled proportions, broad inner chord, rounded tapered hand-wing outline.
photographs.uncertain: Faint annotations and the inconsistent 3.135 ft entry are not numerical inputs.
photographs.completion: 14 m span; central hinge clearance, piecewise elliptical taper and area-normalized chord from the supplied helper.

photographs.reading: Göttingen 417a curved-plate chart, several coefficient axes and curves, with Reynolds labels 168000 and 42000.
photographs.used: Different arm and curved outer section treatments; explicit section-coefficient modelling.
photographs.uncertain: Exact ordinate associations, curve digitisation and full-scale extrapolation are not reliable.
photographs.completion: Separate illustrative inner/outer tables, linear alpha interpolation and nominal-AR induced drag are supplied assumptions, not Stanley's measured coefficients.

photographs.reading: Bird flight as a guide to ornithopter design, © 2007 Stanley J.O. Tinn. An ideal sine-wave trajectory and cruising speed/frequency define required vertical forces; candidate wing actions can be compared using steady aerodynamics. Human-carrying powered flight is the aim.
photographs.used: Pilot-carrying engineered airframe and an independent required-versus-candidate force comparison, never a prescribed flight path.
photographs.uncertain: Handwritten historical update is not used as performance evidence.
photographs.completion: 55 kg seated adult, 16 kW motor, finite fuel and strip simulation are engineering additions.

photographs.reading: Straight and level flapping flight cannot be exactly straight: cyclic lift and thrust create a gently undulating trajectory and varying airspeed. Bounding flight and ring-gait wakes are discussed.
photographs.used: Instantaneous force integration permits small wingbeat responses without forcing an ideal trajectory.
photographs.uncertain: Top handwritten revision and missing appendices are not reconstructed.
photographs.completion: Quasi-steady local forces rather than resolved vortex rings or unsteady wake computation.

photographs.reading: Low-speed downstroke lasts longer than recovery; cruise periods become equal. Wing–wishbone–body resonance can reduce inertial power. Candidate wing forces should be matched against required forces; fore/aft acceleration also exists.
photographs.used: Fixed timing-bias linkage settings, spring energy and coupled wing/body inertia; comparison remains diagnostic.
photographs.uncertain: Dense marginal trajectory revisions are not treated as final equations; quoted bird L/D is not imposed on this aircraft.
photographs.completion: theta=phi-b*sin(phi), b=.3 or 0 only on reset, supplied spring and damping coefficients.

photographs.reading: Wing and body masses oscillate about their common CG. Fore/aft wing movement changes CG-to-lift separation and pitching moment, with help from the tail. Arm and hand wings move up/forward on recovery and down/back against the air; fingers/feathers close on recovery.
photographs.used: Local airflow and generalized force work, body-CG reaction, fore/aft sweep, independent articulated arm/hand motion and recovery overlap.
photographs.uncertain: No quantitative mechanical linkage or complete inertial derivation is recoverable from this page.
photographs.completion: Two rigid half-span sliding outer leaves retain all their mass; supplied mass-point helper and two-coordinate Lagrange equations replace unspecified biological mechanics.

photographs.reading: Opening continuation explicitly says reduced area and span on recovery, then local incidences are adjusted; handwritten addition reads 'and camber'. Later goshawk sections show different local shapes and printed cambers 13%, 10%, 9%, 6%.
photographs.used: Exposure, incidence and camber are separate variables; actual curved geometry changes with camber.
photographs.uncertain: The goshawk's dimensions and percentages are not swan specifications.
photographs.completion: Supplied small camber curves and twist curves are explicit mechanical hypotheses, not samples digitised from these drawings.

photographs.reading: Arm thickness is 5–6%; outer hand is effectively a thin slotted curved plate. At low speed steep local motion rotates lift/drag into forward and vertical components. Partial recovery closure removes tip area/drag. Conventional tail, fin/rudder or weight shift are compatible. Takeoff wing angles and frequency changes describe birds.
photographs.used: 5.5% arm thickness metadata, thin curved sliding hand leaves, conventional long-arm stabilizer/elevator/fin/rudder, resolved local force direction.
photographs.uncertain: Bird takeoff angles, 10% frequency increase and conjectured 20% stiffness increase are not imposed as an aircraft control schedule.
photographs.completion: Three-wheel ground reduction and finite pilot controls; no free takeoff leap or automatic frequency schedule.

photographs.reading: Glide baseline power is Dg*V, with imperial division by 550 for horsepower. Flapping adds aerodynamic, fore/aft, vertical and wing-inertia terms; ideal undamped inertia can exchange energy. Appendix 12 is referenced but absent.
photographs.used: Aerodynamic dissipation, engine work, transmission/damping heat and pilot work are separately integrated. Springs store and return energy, never provide net fuel-free propulsion.
photographs.uncertain: Marginal dimensional notes and unavailable design algorithm are not fabricated.
photographs.completion: Finite shaft torque and 85% transmission; BSFC and idle consumption; RK2 numerical integration of actual translation and coupled coordinates.

engineering.allocations: Full supplied component budget exported unchanged through parameters.mass_budget.
engineering.stability: Supplied passive pitch damping 1000 N m s/rad is a declared engineering addition; no neutral-input pitch or altitude autopilot.
engineering.motor_off: Throttle removal coasts the same spring/inertia/air mechanism. It does not enter frozen glide.
engineering.glide: Separate deliberately initialized extended, frozen, unpowered configuration uses the supplied derived glide trim, not the Approach preset.
engineering.approach: Host preset is already-powered 16 m/s flight, pitch .1, omega 6, 90% throttle and low-speed timing bias. Its kinetic energy belongs to the initial state.
engineering.rendering: Production leaf meshes use makePanel and host-mounted wingPose. Material-coordinate ribs and spars track those same curves. Actual tyre geometry has a baked lateral z axle and spins around z.

limitations: Favourable lightweight mass budget is not a structural substantiation or human-flight safety assessment.
No CFD, flexible aeroelasticity, unsteady wakes, stall hysteresis, leaf-overlap flow or section pitching moments.
Longitudinal moving-mass coupling is represented; roll/yaw inertial coupling is omitted as specified.
Ground contact is a reduced three-wheel constraint, not a suspension model. Rolling and braking dissipate energy; touchdown impulses are not an elastic bounce model.
Detailed tubes, spring housings and cockpit are visual engineering completions. No claim Stanley specified these materials, engine, pilot or numerical tables.
No execution, preview, test or empirical flight verification was performed under the file-only protocol.
